text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,349.65, down 1.75% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 fell 1.41%. The sell‑off was fairly wide‑ranged – 133 stocks advanced against 360 declines, giving a breadth score of 62.2 (rated “HEALTHY”). Both major indices stayed below their 20‑day (63.4% above) and 50‑day (55.9% above) moving averages, and the 200‑day level sits at 23,997.45, well under current prices.  

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding INR 5,672.99 crore, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 2,760.12 crore, extending an 18‑day buying streak for FIIs and a 4‑day selling streak for DIIs. The options market shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.74 for Nifty and 0.71 for Bank Nifty, indicating slightly more call than put interest. Max‑pain points sit near the current levels (Nifty 25,350; Bank Nifty 62,500) with a call wall at 25,400 and a put wall at 25,300, suggesting resistance around those points.  

Watch the 20‑day and 50‑day moving averages for support, and the pivot resistance at 25,562 (Nifty) and 63,441 (Bank Nifty). A break below the 20‑day average or the put wall could trigger further downside, while a hold above the call wall may limit losses. Keep an eye on global cues – especially US tech volatility – as they continue to influence Indian sentiment.
